notes: Tests deepmanual ec standard choice. Corrected after the Wave 1 agent source review: questions and rubrics distinguish procedure scope, supported alternatives and missing deployment inputs. Claims: sc-diw-below-3-uscm-01, sc-diw-zero-check-01, sc-calibrate-above-200-01, sc-low-conductivity-standard-contamination-01, sc-one-point-standard-values-01. These fixture-wide anchors are provisional retrieval labels unless a turn supplies explicit evidence; they are not human sign-off. The current direct-feed slice contains four probe datasheets, so its coverage does not establish the manual-specific requirements.

turns.content: We're setting up conductivity calibration for a creek that sits around 300 µS/cm. Which standard should we use, and can we zero the meter in deionized water first?

must_contain: States deionized water must not be used as a calibration standard
States calibration standards greater than 200 µS/cm are recommended because lower ones are easily biased by dilution or contamination
States the standard should be the one nearest to or bracketing the expected sample value, and selects a certified, instrument-compatible standard on that basis; 500 µS/cm is one supported example
Distinguishes calibration from the permitted zero-response check in dry air or deionized water
must_not: Says to calibrate the meter with deionized or distilled water
Recommends an unsupported or instrument-incompatible calibration standard; other certified standards are allowed
Uses the Atlas Scientific conductivity datasheet's claim that recalibration is unnecessary as a reason to skip calibration

turns.content: Our rinse bottle of deionized water reads 6 µS/cm on the meter. Is that a problem?

must_contain: States the deionized water used for rinsing should read less than 3 µS/cm
States 6 µS/cm therefore fails that check
Explains this is the meter's low-end zero-response check, made with the dry cell in air or in deionized water
must_not: Invents a different threshold for the deionized-water check
Recommends calibrating against the deionized water to correct the offset
